It seems, we all perpetrated a similar iniquity for we have all in the like manner, met with widowhood.

units.sanskrit: त्वया स्वर्गप्रतिच्छन्दैर् लालिताः स्म रतिप्रियाः । त्वयि कामवशाः सर्वाः स नस् त्यज्य क्व गच्छसि ॥ अस्माकं त्वम् अनाथानां नाथो ह्य् असि सुरोपम । प्रतिवाक्यं जगन्नाथ दातुम् अर्हसि मानद ॥ गमनं ते महाराज दारुणं प्रतिभाति नः ॥ नूनं कान्ततराः कान्त तस्मिंल् लोके वरस्त्रियः । ततस् त्वं प्रस्थितो वीर विहायेमं गृहे जनम् ॥ किं नु ते करुणं वीर भार्यास्व् एतासु भूमिप । अहो निष्करुणा यात्रा नराणाम् और्ध्वदेहिकी । ये परित्यज्य दारान् स्वान् निरपेक्षा व्रजन्ति ह ॥
units.english: Alas! We were all fond of thee and thou didst take care of us with heavenly enjoyments. Casting us off where dost thou go now ? lord of the world, giver of honors, thou resembling a celestial, thou art our master who have been separated from their lord. lord, we are bewailing like hind; it behoves thee to give us a reply. lord sovereign, thy departure, making thy kinsmen sorrowful and thy wives bewail, appears to us as terribly hard. Forsooth it appears lord, that the damsels of the other world are more beautiful, because, hero, thou hast departed leaving behind thy own people. What is the reason hero, that thou dost pay no heed to the lamentations of thy wives. Alas, the march of men to the other world is ruthless, because without caring for them they even forsake their own wives.

units.sanskrit: अपतित्वं स्त्रियाः श्रेयो न तु शूरः स्त्रियाः पतिः । स्वर्गस्त्रीणां प्रियाः शुरास् तेषाम् अपि च ताः प्रियाः ॥
units.english: It is better for women not to have husbands than beloved, heroic husbands, because they love the women of the celestial region and they too are fond of heroes.

units.sanskrit: अहो क्षिप्रम् अदृश्येन नयता त्वया रणप्रियम् । जरासंधबलं जित्वा हत्वा राज्ञां च संयुगे । जित्वा देवगणं युद्धे यक्षान् अपि च संयुगे । कथं मानुषमात्रेण हतस् त्वं जगतीपते ॥
units.english: Alas! carrying away imperceptibly such a heroic husband Death has pierced our very vitals. lord of the world, having slain the army of Jarāsandha and vanquished the other enemies in battle why hast thou met with death at the hands of an ordinary man ? Alas! Fighting with Indra in a combat of arrows thou wert not defeated by the immortals.

units.sanskrit: अमर्त्यैर् अजितो युद्धे मर्त्येनासि कथं हतः ॥ त्वया सागरम् अक्षोख्यं विक्षोभ्य शरवृष्टिभिः । रत्नसर्वस्वहरणं जित्वा पाशधरं कृतम् ॥
units.english: How hast thou been then slain by a mortal ? Having agitated, with a shower of arrows, the ocean that is incapable of being moved thou didst conquer Varuna the holder of the noose, and take away all his riches.

units.sanskrit: त्वया पौरजनास्यार्थे मन्दं वर्षति वासवे । सायकैर् जलदान् भित्त्वा बलाद् वर्षं प्रवर्तितम् ॥
units.english: When Vāsava did not pour profuse showers, thou didst, for the citizens, bore through the clouds with thy arrows and bring down rain by force.

units.sanskrit: प्रतापावनताः सर्वे तव तिष्ठन्ति पार्थिवाः । प्रेषयाणा वरार्हाणि रत्नान्य् आच्छादनानि च ॥
units.english: By thy prowess all kings were humiliated and used to send thee the precious jewels and clothes.

units.sanskrit: तवैवं देवकल्पस्य दृष्टवीर्यस्य शत्रुभिः । कथं प्राणान्तिकं घोरम् ईदृशं भयम् आगतम् ॥ प्राप्ताः स्मो विधवाशब्दं त्वयि नाथे निपातिते । यद्य् एवं नाथ गन्तव्यं यदि वा विस्मृता वयम् । वाक्यमात्रेण यास्येति कर्तव्यो नः परिग्रहः ॥ प्रसीद नाथ भीताः स्म पादौ ते याम मूर्धभिः । अलं दूरप्रवासेन निवर्त मथुराधिप ॥
units.english: Alas, thy manliness was manifest unto thy enemies and thou wert like a god. How has then such a life-ending calamity befallen thee ? Thyself being slain lord, we are passing by the name of widows. Although not mad we have become so and have been assailed by death. lord, if thou wert determined upon departing why hast thou then forgotten us? Would it have tired thee if thou hadst say it in mere words ? lord, king of Mathurā, we bow unto thy feet in fear. Be thou propitiated and return from the distant land.

units.sanskrit: अहो वीर कथं शेषे निषण्णस् तृणपांसुषु । शयानस्य हि ते भूमौ कस्मान् नोद्विजते मनः ॥ केन सुप्तप्रहारो ऽयं दत्तो ऽस्माकम् अतर्कितः । किं वयं सति गन्तव्ये सह भर्त्रा रुदामहे ॥ एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे दीना कंसमाता प्रवेपती । क्व मे वत्सः क्व मे पुत्र इति रोरूयते भृशम् ॥
units.english: hero, how dost thou lie down on grass and dust? Prostrating thyself on earth does not thy body feel any inconvenience ? Alas, who has inflicted on us this stroke of sleep? Who has ruthlessly struck the body of these women ? The woman, who has to survive, should weep and repent. Why should we weep when we are to follow our husband ? In the meantime trembling poorly and crying aloud Where is my son? Where is my child? Kansa's mother arrived there.

units.sanskrit: सापश्यत् तं हतं पुत्रं निपीतं शशिनं यथा । हृदयेन विदीर्णेन श्राम्यमाणा पुनः पुनः ॥ पुत्रं समभिवीक्षन्ती हा हतास्मीति वाशती । कृत्वा पुत्रेति करुणं विललापार्तया गिरा ॥ पुत्र शूरव्रते युक्त ज्ञातीनां नन्दिवर्धन । किम् इदं त्वरितं तात प्रस्थानं कृतवान् असि ॥ प्रसुप्तश् चासि विवृते किं पुत्र शयनं विना । रावणेन पुरा गीतः श्लोको ऽयं साधुसंमतः । बलज्येष्ठेन लोकेषु राक्षसानां समागमे ॥
units.english: Beholding her son like unto the moon shorn of its lustre her heart as if broke assunder and she repeatedly lost her consciousness. Beholding her son and exclaiming Alas! am undone! she began to bewail along with her daughters-in-law. Placing on her lap the head of her son, that one, fond of sons, began to bewail plaintively saying my son, thou the enhancer of the delight of thy kinsmen, thou ever devoted to the vow of a hero, why hast thou departed so soon? my son observant of vows, why art thou asleep before all men? The kings should never lie down on earth in this way –. When in the days of yore all the Rākshasas assembled Rāvana, the foremost of the strong in all the worlds, uttered the following verse, spoken well of by the sages.

units.sanskrit: बान्धवेभ्यो भयं घोरम् अनिवार्यं भविष्यति ॥ तथैव ज्ञातिलुब्धस्य मम पुत्रस्य धीमतः । ज्ञातिभ्यो भयम् उत्पन्नं शरीरान्तकरं महत् ॥
units.english: Although am of great strength and a destroyer of the immortals, a terrible and irresistable calamity will proceed to me from my kinsmen. And such a life-destroying great calamity will also proceed to my intelligent son from my relatives .

units.sanskrit: सा पतिं भूपतिं वृद्धम् उग्रसेनं विचेतसम् । उवाच रुदती वाक्यं विवत्सा सौरभी यथा ॥
units.english: Thereupon weeping like unto a cow, separated from her calf, she said to her husband the old king Ugrasena.

units.sanskrit: एह्य् एहि राजन् धर्मात्मन् पश्य पुत्रं जनेश्वरम् । अस्य कुर्मो महाराज निर्याणसदृशीं क्रियाम् । प्रेतत्वम् उपपन्नस्य गतस्य यमसादनम् ॥
units.english: Come and see, pious king, this thy royal son is lying on the bed of a hero like a mountain clapped by a thunderbolt. king, you are to perform the obsequial rites of this thy son who has repaired to the abode of Death and attained to the state of a ghost.

units.sanskrit: वीरभोज्यानि राज्यानि वयं चापि पराजिताः । गच्छ विज्ञाप्यतां कृष्णः कंससंस्कारकारणात् ॥
units.english: Kingdoms are worthy of being enjoyed by heroes and we have been defeated. Go and ask Krishna about Kansha's funeral rites.

units.sanskrit: मरणान्तानि वैराणि शान्ते शान्तिर् भविष्यति । इमास् ते किं करिष्यन्ति भार्या राजन् सुखोचिताः । अहं ते जननी पुत्र किमर्थं नाभिभाषसे । प्रस्थितो दीर्घम् अध्वानं परित्यज्य्य प्रियं जनम् ॥
units.english: Enmity terminates with death—it ceases with the death of the enemy. His obsequial rites should therefore be performed. hero, the inevitable Death has, against the knowledge of this unfortunate woman, taken away a son like thee well-read in moral laws.

units.sanskrit: नामानि च गृहीतानि सम्यग्वृत्तानि तैर् गुणैः । रुदन्ति तव भृत्यानां कुलानि कुलयूथप ॥
units.english: the master of thy clan, thy servants, who were pleased with thy qualities on receiving honors and various presents from thee, are now weeping.

units.sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल दीर्घबाहो महाबल । त्राहि दीनं जनं सर्वं पुरम् अन्तःपुरं तथा ॥ रुदतीनाम् भृशार्तानां कंसस्त्रीणां सविस्तरम् । जगामास्तं दिनकरः संध्यारागेण रञ्जितः ॥ वैशंपायन उवाच उग्रसेनस् तु कृष्णस्य समीपं दुःखितो ययौ । स ददर्श गृहे कृष्णं यादवैर् अभिसंवृतम् । कृष्णः प्रोवाच निखिलं सर्वेषाम् उपशृण्वताम् । अहो मयातिबाल्येन नररोषानुवर्तिना । वैधव्यं स्त्रीसहस्राणां कंसस्यास्य कृते कृतम् ॥
units.english: foremost of kings, thou of large arms and great strength, rise up and save the people of thy house and other poor men. While the wives of Kansa, stricken with great misery, were thus bewailing the sun, smitten with evening rays, set in. Vaishampayana said:—Breathing like a person who has drunk poison, Ugrasena, burning with grief for his son, approached Krishna. He saw him there encircled by Yadavas repenting for his sinful destruction of Kansa. Hearing the heart-rending lamentations of Kansa's wives he, censuring his own self in that assembly of the Yādavas, said :—Alas, out of my childish freak and under the influence of anger, have, by the destruction of Kansa, made widows of these thousand women.

units.sanskrit: कारुण्यं खलु नारीषु प्राकृतस्यापि जायते । एवम् आर्तं रुदन्तीषु मया भर्तरि पातिते ॥
units.english: On the death of their husband these women are bewailing so very plaintively that even an ordinary man's heart, on hearing it, feels compassion.

units.sanskrit: कृतान्तस्यानभिज्ञातः स्त्रीणां कारुण्यसंभवः ॥ कंसस्य हि वधः श्रेयान् प्राग् एवाभिमतो मम । सुताम् उद्वेजनीयस्य पापेष्व् अभिरतस्य च ॥
units.english: Hearing the lamentations of these guileless women, even Kritānta's Regent of the dead heart is filled with pity. had determined before that Kansa, the oppresser of the pious, and always given to vice, should be slain.

units.sanskrit: लोके पतितवृत्तस्य पुरुषस्याल्पमेधसः । अक्लिष्टं मरणं श्रेयो न विद्विष्टस्य जीवितम् ॥
units.english: Death is preferable to life unto him who, in this world, is of a degraded conduct, ruthless temper, feeble understanding and whom the people hate.

units.sanskrit: कंसः पापरतिश् चैव साधूनां चाप्य् असंमतः । धिक्शब्दपतितश् चैव जीविते चास्य का दया ॥ स्वर्गे तपोभृतां वासः फलं पुण्यस्य कर्मणः । इहापि यशसा युक्तस् तत्रस्थैर् उपधार्यते ॥
units.english: Kansa was highly sinful, never liked by the pious and him every one used to hate. What pity should then be felt for him ? The ascetics, as a fruit of their virtuous deeds, live in the celestial region. He, who attains to glory in this world, is also like a dweller in heaven to.

units.sanskrit: नरा धर्मप्रवृत्ताश् च न नृपो विकृतो भवेत् ॥ गुणेषु दुष्टवृत्तानां कृत्तान्तः कुरुते पदम् । अतीव देवा रक्षन्ति नरं धर्मपरायणम् । कर्तारः सुलभा लोके दुष्कृतस्येह कर्मणः ॥
units.english: If the subjects are self-controlled, observant of their own duties and perform pious deeds, unrighteousness can never touch the king. Those, who are wicked, are constrained by Death to reap the proper fruits. The pious attain to auspicious fruits in the next world. Many are the agents of impious deeds in these worlds and therefore the gods perfectly protect the pious.

units.sanskrit: हतः सो ऽयं मया कंसः साध्व् एतद् अवगम्यताम् । पौराश् च पुर्यां श्रेण्यश् च सान्त्व्यतां सर्व एव हि ॥
units.english: That Kansa has been slain by me should be considered by you as righteous for have eradicated thereby his mis-deeds. Do you now console the sorrowful women, the citizens and the merchants.

units.sanskrit: उग्रसेनो महातेजाः कृष्णम् अस्राविलेक्षणम् । प्रलपन्तं जगामैवं यादवानां च संसदि । उग्रसेनो यदून् गृह्य पुत्रकिल्बिषशङ्कितः ॥
units.english: When Krishna said this, Ugrasena, out of fear for his son's misdeeds, entered lowering his head along with other Yadavas.

units.sanskrit: स कृष्णं पुण्डरीकाक्षम् उवाच यदुसंसदि । बाष्पसंदिग्धया वाचा दीनया सज्जमानया ॥ पुत्र निर्यातितः क्रोधो नीतो याम्यां दिशं रिपुः । स्वधर्माधिगता कीर्तिर् नाम विश्रावितं भुवि ॥
units.english: In that assembly of the Yadus he addressed to the lotus-eyed Krishna the following poor words, sullied by the vapour of grief and becoming the occasion :— my son, your anger has been pacified, your enemy has been led to the abode of Yama, your glory has followed your own duties and your name has become celebrated in this world.

units.sanskrit: स्थापितं सत्सु माहात्म्यं शङ्किता रिपवः कृताः । स्थापितो यादवो वंशो गर्विताः सुहृदः कृताः ॥
units.english: By this action you have established your glory amongst the pious, terrified your enemies, made strong the position of the Yādavas and rendered your friends proud.

units.sanskrit: सामन्तेषु नरेन्द्रेषु प्रतापस् ते प्रकाशितः । मित्राणि त्वां भजिष्यन्ति संश्रयिष्यन्ति चार्थिनः ॥
units.english: Your glory has spread itself amongst the neighbouring chiefs and now they will all seek alliance with you and your friendship.

units.sanskrit: प्रकृतयो ऽनुयास्यन्ति स्तोष्यन्ति त्वां द्विजातयः । संधिविग्रहमुख्यास् त्वां प्रणमिष्यन्ति मन्त्रिणः ॥
units.english: hero, your subjects will be devoted to you, the Brāhmanas will sing your glories and the ministers, well read in peace and dissension making, will bow unto you.

units.sanskrit: प्रतिगृहाण कृष्णेदं कंसस्य बलम् अव्ययम् ॥
units.english: Krishna, accept this immortal army of Kansa abounding in elephants, horses, chariots and infantry.

units.sanskrit: धनं धान्यं च यत् किंचिद् रत्नान्य् आच्छादनानि च । एवं हि विहिते योगे पर्याप्ते कृष्ण विग्रहे । प्रतिष्ठितायां मेदिन्यां यदूनां शत्रुसूदन ॥
units.english: Mādhava, let your men take Kansa's wealth, corn, jewels, covers, gold, clothes, women and all that he possessed. Krishna, the slayer of your enemies, by the Yoga, to which you have resorted on behalf of the Yādavas, all dissensions have been put a stop to and the earth has been established.

units.sanskrit: त्वं गतिश् चागतिश् चैव यदूनां यदुनन्दन । शृणु तद् ब्रुवतां वीर कृपणानाम् इदं वचः । अस्य त्वत्क्रोधदग्धस्य कंसस्याशुभकर्मणः । तव प्रसादाद् गोविन्दे प्रेतकार्यं क्रियते ह ॥
units.english: descendant of Yadu, from you now will proceed the happiness or misery of the Yadavas. Hear, what they are saying with a depressed heart. If you please, Govinda, they may perform the obsequial rites of Kansa, of sinful deeds, who has been consumed by the fire of your anger.

units.sanskrit: अस्य कृत्वा नरेन्द्रस्य विपन्नस्यौर्ध्वदेहिकम् । सस्नुषो ऽहं सभार्यश् च चरिष्यामि मृगैः सह ॥
units.english: Having performed the after-death ceremonies of that king who has met with this calamity, shall, along with my wife and daughters-in-law, range in the forest with the animals.

units.sanskrit: प्रेतसंस्कारमात्रेण कृते बान्धवकर्मणि । आनृण्यं लौकिकं कृष्ण गतः किल भवाम्य् अहम् ॥
units.english: To perform the obsequial rites of the dead is the duty of men –. By performing this, Krishna, people are freed from their social obligations.

units.sanskrit: अस्याग्निं पश्चिमं दत्त्वा चित्तिस्थाने विधिं विना । तोयप्रदानमात्रेण कंसस्यानृण्यम् आप्नुयाम् ॥
units.english: Therefore having made his funeral pyre, putting fire to it and offering oblation of water shall have discharged debt to Kansa.

units.sanskrit: एतन् मे कृष्ण विज्ञाप्यं स्नेहो ऽत्र मम युज्यताम् । प्राप्नोतु सुगतिं तत्र कृपणः पश्चिमां क्रियाम् ॥
units.english: This is my only prayer, Krishna. Show me kindness in this matter. With the performance of his after-death rites let sinful Kansa attain to a blessed state.

units.sanskrit: एतच् छ्रुत्वा वचस् तस्य कृष्णः परमहर्षितः । सदृशं राजशार्दूल वृत्तस्य च कुलस्य च ।
units.english: Hearing the words of Ugrasena, Krishna was filled with surprise. And consoling him he said. sire, foremost of kings, what you have said behoves your age and family and becomes your nature.

units.sanskrit: कुले महति ते जन्म वेदान् विदितवान् असि । कथं न ज्ञायते तात नियतिर् दुरतिक्रमा ॥ स्थावराणां च भूतानां जङ्गमानां च पार्थिव । पूर्वजन्मकृतं कर्म कालेन परिपच्यते ॥
units.english: sire, you are born in a great race and know every thing that should be known. Why do you not then understand that destiny is inevitable ? king, pristine deeds of all creatures, mobile and immobile, attain to fullness in time.

units.sanskrit: श्रुतवन्तो ऽर्थवन्तश् च दातारः प्रियदर्शनाः । ब्रह्मण्या नयसंपन्ना दीनानुग्रहकारिणः ॥ लोकपालसमास् तात महेन्द्रसमविक्रमाः । धार्मिकाः सर्वभावज्ञाः प्रजापालनतत्पराः । क्षत्रधर्मपरा दान्ताः कालेन निधनं गताः ॥
units.english: foremost of kings, even the liberal, beautiful and rich sovereigns, always kind to the poor, endued with prowess like that of Mahendra, well read in Srutis, laws and knowledge of Brahman, and like unto the regents of quarters, are carried away by Death –. You know too that many a pious king, ever intent on protecting their subjects, devoted to Kshitriya dutes, self-controlled and well-read in all, meet with death in time.

units.sanskrit: स्वयम् एव कृतं कर्म शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम् । प्राप्ते काले तु तत् कर्म दृश्यते सर्वदेहिनाम् ॥
units.english: When the proper time comes men, by enjoyment or suffering, can understand whether his actions have been good or bad.

units.sanskrit: एषा ह्य् अन्तर्हिता माया दुर्विज्ञेया सुरैर् अपि । यथायं मुह्यते लोको ह्य् अत्र कर्मैव कारणम् ॥
units.english: king, even the gods cannot understand the true nature of Māyā that exists in the hearts of all. Karma is the instrument of people's being stupified thereby.

units.sanskrit: कालेनाभिहतः कंसः पूर्वकर्मप्रचोदितः । न ह्य् अयं कारणं तत्र कालः कर्म च कारणम् ॥
units.english: Urged on by his pristine deeds Kansa has met with death in time; am not the cause thereof. Karma pristine action and Kāla Time are the instruments thereof.

units.sanskrit: सूर्यसोममयं तात कृत्स्नं स्थावरजङ्गमम् । कालेन निधनं गत्वा कालेनैव च जायते । तस्मात् सर्वाणि भूतानि कालस्य वशगानि वै ॥
units.english: This universe, consisting of the sun and moon, mobile and immobile creations, meets with dissolution in time and springs up into existence again in time. Time subdues and favours all and therefore all the creatures are subject to time.

units.sanskrit: स्वदोषेणैव दग्धस्य सूनोस् तव नराधिप । नाहं वै कारणं तत्र कालस् तत्र तु कारणम् ॥
units.english: king, your son has been consumed by his own sin. am not the instrument thereof but Time is the cause.

units.sanskrit: पलायनपरः कालः किं करिष्यत्य् अकारणम् । कालस् तु बलवान् राजन् दुर्विज्ञेया हि सा गतिः ॥
units.english: Your son has been slain by his own actions; am surely the instrument no doubt. Powerful is Time and it is difficult to know its course.

units.sanskrit: परावरविशेषज्ञा यां यान्ति समदर्शिनः । गतिः कालस्य सा येन सर्वं कालस्य गोचरम् । ब्रवीमि यद् अहं तात तद् अनुष्ठीयतां वचः ॥
units.english: This is known to persons who impartially look into the essence of things. That is the course of Time by which everything comes within its ken. Let it go, do what say now.

units.sanskrit: न हि राज्येन मे कार्यं नाप्य् अहं राज्यलालसः । किं तु लोकहितार्थाय कीर्त्यर्थं च सुतस् तव । व्यङ्गभूतः कुलस्यास्य सानुजो विनिपातितः ॥
units.english: do not care for the kingdom or the royal throne. did not slay Kansa for a territory. For the behoof of all the worlds and for establishing my glory your son, the curse of this family, has been slain by me along with all his attendants.

units.sanskrit: अहं स एव गोमध्ये गोपैः सह वनेचरः । प्रीतिमान् विचरिष्यामि कामचारी यथा गजः ॥
units.english: Like unto a bird coursing at will, shall again delightedly range in the forest in the midst of kine along with the Gopas.

units.sanskrit: एतावच् छतशो ऽप्य् एवं सत्येन प्रब्रवीमि ते । न मे कार्यं नृपत्वेन विज्ञाप्यं क्रियताम् इदम् ॥ भवान् राजास्तु मे मान्यो यदूनाम् अग्रणीः प्रभुः । विजयायाभिषिच्यस्व स्वराज्ये राजसत्तम ॥
units.english: foremost of kings, swear a hundred times, that stand in no need of the kingdom. Communicate this to all foremost of kings, you are the leader and the lord of the Yadavas and therefore deserve respect from me. Therefore place yourself on the throne and acquire victory by becoming the king.

units.sanskrit: यदि ते मत्प्रियं कार्यं यदि वा नास्ति ते व्यथा । मया निसृष्टं राज्यं स्वं चिराय प्रतिगृह्यताम् ॥
units.english: If you think it proper to do what pleases me, and if it does not pain you, do you accept for ever this kingdom abdicated by me.

units.sanskrit: वैशंपायन उवाच एतच् छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं नोत्तरं प्रत्यभाषत । अभिषेकेण गोविन्दो योजयाम् आस योगवित् ॥
units.english: Vaishampāyana said:—Hearing those words of Krishna in the assembly of Yadus Ugrasena bent down his head in bashfulness and could give no reply. Then Govinda, well read in laws, installed him on the throne.

units.sanskrit: स बद्धमुकुटः श्रीमान् उग्रसेनो महीपतिः । चकार सह कृष्णेन कंसस्य निधनक्रियाम् ॥
units.english: With the crown on his head the beautiful and effulgent king Ugrasena, along with Krishna, performed the funeral ceremonies of Kansa.

units.sanskrit: तं सर्वे यादवा मुख्या राजानं कृष्णशासनात् । अनुजग्मुः पुरीमार्गे देवा इव शतक्रतुम् ॥
units.english: As the celestials follow their king Indra so all the leading Yadavas, at the command of Krishna, followed Ugrasena in the high-way of the city.

units.sanskrit: रजन्यां तु प्रभातायां ततः सूर्ये चिरोदिते । पश्चिमं कंससंस्कारं चक्रुस् ते यदुपुंगवाः ॥
units.english: Thereupon when the night passed away and the sun rose, the leading Yadavas began to perform the funeral ceremonies of Kansa.

units.sanskrit: शिबिकायां समारोप्य कंसदेहं यथाक्रमम् । नैष्ठिकेन विधानेन चक्रुस् ते तस्य सत्क्रियाम् ॥ स नीतो यमुनातीरम् उत्तरं नृपतेः सुतः । संस्कृतश् च यथान्यायं नैधनेन चिताग्निना ॥ तथैव भ्रातरं चास्य सुनामानं महाभुजम् । संस्कारं लम्भयाम् आसुः सह कृष्णेन यादवाः ॥ अक्षयं चापि प्रेतेभ्यो भाषमाणाः प्रतस्थिरे ॥ तयोस् ते सलिलं दत्त्वा यादवा दीनमानसाः । पुरस्कृत्योग्रसेनं वै विविषुर् मथुरां पुरीम् ॥ सर्वान् स्वजातिसंबन्धान् दिग्भ्यः कंसभयार्दितान् । यदुवृष्ण्यन्धकमधु दाशार्हकुकुरादिकान् ॥ वैशंपायन उवाच स कृष्णस् तत्र बलवान् रौहिणेयेन संगतः । प्राप्तयौवनदेहस् तु युक्तो राजश्रिया ज्वलन् । चकार मथुरां वीरह्. स रत्नाकरभूषणाम् ॥ कस्यचित् त्व् अथ कालस्य सहितौ रामकेशवौ । गुरुं संदीपनिं काश्यम् अवन्तिपुरवासिनम् । धनुर्वेदचिकीर्षार्थम् उभौ ताव् अभिजग्मतुः ॥
units.english: Thereupon desirous of performing the obsequial rites of king Kansa according to the ritualastic laws they placed his body in a palanquin and took it to the northern bank of Yamunā. And in due order they performed his funeral rites by setting fire to the pyre –. With the consent of Krishna the Yādavas also performed the funeral ceremonies of the large-armed brother of Kansa by name Sunāma. Then repeatedly exclaiming. May the departed attain to an eternal course the Vrishnis, Andhakas and Yadavas offered oblations of water in their honor. Having then offered water to Kansa and his brother, all the Yadavas, preceded by Ugrasena, returned to Mathura with a sorrowful heart. Vaishampayana said:—Thereupon united with Rohini's son the heroic and powerful Krishna began to live in the city of Mathurā filled with Yadavas. Gradually his body began to shine in royal and youthful grace and he began to range in the city of Mathurā adorned with the ocean-like Yamunā. After a few days, with a view to learn Danurveda science of war Rāma and Krishna, adorned with vedic study and good conduct, went to this preceptor Sāndipani of the city of Avanti in the province of Kashi and communicated to him their family -.

units.sanskrit: निवेद्य गोत्रं स्वाध्यायाम् आचारेणाभ्यलंकृतौ । शुश्रूशू निरहंकाराव् उभौ रामजनार्दनौ । तौ च श्रुतिधरौ वीरौ यथावत् प्रतिपद्यताम् । अहोरात्रैश् चतुःषष्ट्या साङ्गं वेदम् अधीयताम् ॥
units.english: When they, shorn of pride began to serve him he recognised Janārddana and Rāma as his pupils and began to instruct them in that useful science. The heroic Rāma and Janārddana could learn anything as soon as they heard it; and therefore within sixty-four days and nights they studied and mastered all the Vedas with their various Angas.

units.sanskrit: सरहस्यं धनुर्वेदं सकलं ताव् अवाप्नुताम् । अचिरेणैव कालेन गुरुस् ताव् अभ्यषिक्षयत् ॥
units.english: In no time their preceptor taught them Danurveda, consisting of four divisions and the mysterious use of various other weapons.

units.sanskrit: अतीवमानुषीं मेधां तयोश् चिन्त्य गुरुस् तदा । ददर्श च महात्मानाव् उभौ ताव् अपि पर्वसु । पूजयन्तौ महादेवं साक्षात् त्र्यक्षम् अवस्थितम् ॥
units.english: Thinking of their superhuman merit he used to consider them as the moon and the sun. And when he offered adoration to those two high-souled deities in Parva he used to see Siva and Vishnu before him.

units.sanskrit: गुरुं सांदीपनिं कृष्णः कृतकृत्यो ऽभ्यभाषत । गुर्वर्थं किं ददानीति रामेण सह भारत ॥ तयोः प्रभावं स ज्ञात्वा गुरुः प्रोवाच हृष्टवत् । पुत्रम् इच्छाम्य् अहं दत्तं यो मृतो लवणाम्भसि ॥
units.english: Thereupon, descendant of Bharata, having finished their education Baladeva and Krishna said to their preceptor Sāndipani:—What fee shall we offer thee for your acting as our preceptor ? The preceptor knew their power and so with a delighted heart said wish you to return me the son who died in the ocean of salt-water.

units.sanskrit: पुत्र एको हि मे जातः स चापि तिमिना हृतः । प्रभासे तीर्थयात्रायां तं मे त्वं पुनर् आनय ॥
units.english: Krishna, had only one son. When had gone out on a pilgrimage to Pravāsa a Timi fish carried away my son. Do you bring me back my that son.

units.sanskrit: तथेत्य् एवाब्रवीत् कृष्णो रामस्यानुमते स्थितः । गत्वा समुद्रं तेजस्वी विवेशान्तर्जलं हरिः ॥
units.english: With Rāma's consent Krishna said it will be so. And then going to the ocean Hari entered into its water.

units.sanskrit: तम् आह कृष्णः क्वासौ भोः पुत्रः सांदीपनेर् इति ॥ समुद्रस् तम् उवाचेदं दैत्यः पञ्चजनो महान् । तिमिरूपेण तं बालं ग्रस्तवान् इति माधव ॥
units.english: With folded hands the regent of the ocean came to Vāsudeva, who said Where is Sāndipani's son ? The ocean replied, Mādhava, a huge-bodied demon, by name Panchajana, has devoured that boy, in the form of a Timi fish.

units.sanskrit: स पञ्चजनम् आसाद्य जघान पुरुषोत्तमः । न चाससाद तं बालं गुरुपुत्रं तदाच्युतः ॥ स तु पञ्चजनं हत्वा शङ्खं लेभे जनार्दनः । यः स देवमनुष्येषु पाञ्चजन्य इति श्रुतः ॥
units.english: Hearing it the eternal Purusha Achyuta Krishna went to Panchajana and killed him. But he did not get his preceptor's son. The conch, which Janārddana obtained after slaying Panchajana, is known amongst gods and men as Panchajanya.

units.sanskrit: आसनस्थं ततो विष्णुः प्रोवाच यमम् ऊर्जितम् । ततो यमो ऽभ्युपागम्य ववन्दे तं गदाधरम् । तम् उवाचाथ वै कृष्णो गुरुपुत्रः प्रदीयताम् । तयोस् तत्र तदा युद्धम् आसीद् घोरतरं महत् । आनिनाय गुरोः पुत्रं चिरनष्टं यमक्षयात् ॥ ततः सांदीपनेः पुत्रः प्रसादाद् अमितौजसः । दीर्घकालगतः प्रेतः पुनर् आसीच् छरीरवान् ॥
units.english: Thereupon that foremost of Purushas repaired to the abode of Vaivaswan Yama. Then approaching him Yama saluted Gadādhara. Krishna said to him:—Give me my preceptor's son. Thereat there took place a terrible encounter between them both. Thereupon having vanquished the fearful son of Vivaswan, the foremost of Purusha Achyuta obtained the child son of his preceptor. He then brought from Yama's abode his preceptor's son lost for a long time. By the power of Krishna of peerless energy Sāndipani’s son, dead long ago, returned in his bodily form.

units.sanskrit: तद् अशक्यम् अचिन्त्यं च दृष्ट्वा सुमहद् अद्भुतम् । सर्वेषाम् एव भूतानां विस्मयः समजायत ॥
units.english: Beholding this highly wonderful feat which cannot be thought of or performed by any all the creatures were filled with surprise.

units.sanskrit: स गुरोः पुत्रम् आदाय पाञ्चजन्यं च माधवः । रत्नानि च महार्हाणि पुनर् आयाज् जगत्पतिः ॥
units.english: Taking his preceptor's son, Panchajanya and diverse precious jewels, Mādhava, the Lord of the universe, returned –.

units.sanskrit: रक्षसस् तस्य रत्नानि महार्हाणि बहूनि च । आनाय्यावेदयाम् आस गुरवे वासवानुजः ॥
units.english: Having brought all those precious jewels through Yama's servants the Rakshasas Vāsava's younger brother Krishna dedicated them to his preceptor.

units.sanskrit: गदापरिघयुद्धेषु सर्वास्त्रेषु च ताव् उभौ । अचिरान् मुख्यतां प्राप्तौ सर्वलोके धनुर्भृताम् ॥ ततः सांदीपनेः पुत्रं तद्रूपवयसं तदा । चिरनष्टेन पुत्रेण काश्यः सांदीपनिस् तदा । समेत्य मुमुदे राजन् पूजयन् रामकेशवौ ॥
units.english: Having handed over to their preceptor Sāndipani, his son, of the same age and beauty, as before, together with all the jewels the highly intelligent Rāma and Keshava, the foremost of all the warriors, in all the worlds, in the use of clubs, swords and various other weapons, were pleased –. Being greatly pleased with the reconciliation with his son, who had been lost for a long time Kashyas's son Sāndipani honored greatly Rāma and Keshava.

units.sanskrit: कृतास्त्रौ ताव् उभौ वीरौ गुरुम् आमन्त्र्य सुव्रतौ । आयातौ मथुरां भूयो वसुदेवसुताव् उभौ ॥
units.english: Having acquired mastery in the use of all weapons and honored their preceptor, those two vow-observing and heroic sons of Vasudeva returned to Mathurā.

units.sanskrit: ततः प्रत्युद्ययुः सर्वे यादवा यदुनन्दनौ । सबाला हृष्टमनस उग्रसेनपुरोगमाः ॥
units.english: Hearing of the approach of the two scions of the Yadu race, all the Yādavas, boys and old men, headed by Ugrasena, delightedly went out of the city to receive them.

units.sanskrit: सबालवृद्धा सा चैव पुरी समभिवर्तत ॥
units.english: All the subjects, old and young, the priests and the ministers stood before the city in rows.

units.sanskrit: नन्दितूर्याण्य् अवाद्यन्त तुष्टुवुश् च जनार्दनम् । रथ्याः पताकामालिन्यो भ्राजन्ति स्म समन्ततः ॥
units.english: Bugles were sounded, people began to chant the glories of Janārddana, and all the streets were adorned with flags and garlands.

units.sanskrit: गोविन्दागमने ऽत्यर्थं यथैवेन्द्रमहे तथा ॥
units.english: With Govinda's return all the houses were filled with joy as on the occasion of an Indra-Yajna.

units.sanskrit: मुदिताश् चाप्य् अगायन्त राजमार्गेषु गायनाः । स्तवाशीःप्रथमा गाथा यादवानां प्रियंकराः ॥ गोविन्दरामौ संप्राप्तौ भ्रातरौ लोकविश्रुतौ । स्वे पुरे निर्भयाः सर्वे क्रीडध्वं सह बान्धवैः ॥
units.english: The songsters began to sing, in high ways, songs of blessings and eulogy, highly liked by the Yadavas. They made the announcement, The two brothers, Rāma and Govinda, celebrated all over the world, have returned to their city. Let all fearlessly sport with their friends.

units.sanskrit: न तत्र कश् चिद् दीनो वा मलिनो वा विचेतनः । मथुरायां बभौ राजन् गोविन्दे समुपस्थिते ॥ वयांसि साधुवाक्यानि प्रहृष्टा गोहयद्विपाः । नरनारीगणाः सर्वे भेजिरे मनसः सुखम् ॥
units.english: king, when Govinda arrived at Mathurā, there was none who was poorly, sorrowful or insensible. The birds began to pour sweet notes, and the horses, elephants and cows were all cheerful. And men and women attained to mental felicity.

units.sanskrit: शिवाश् च वाताः प्रववुर् विरजस्का दिशो दश । दैवतानि च सर्वाणि हृष्टान्य् आयतनेष्व् अपि ॥
units.english: Delightful winds began to blow and the ten quarters were freed from dust and all the tutelary deities in the temples became delighted.

units.sanskrit: तानि सर्वाण्य् अदृश्यन्त पुरीं प्राप्ते जनार्दने ॥
units.english: What more when Janārddana arrived at the city all the signs, that were visible in the golden age, appeared there.

units.sanskrit: ततः काले शिवे पुण्ये स्यन्दनेनारिमर्दनः । हरियुक्तेन गोविन्दो विवेश मथुरां पुरीम् ॥ अनुजग्मुर् यदुगणाः शक्रं देवगणा इव ॥ वसुदेवस्य भवनं ततस् तौ यदुनन्दनौ । प्रविष्टौ हृष्टवदनौ चन्द्रादित्याव् इवाचलम् ॥ ताव् आयुधानि विन्यस्य गृहे स्वे स्वैरचारिणौ । मुमुदाते यदुवरौ वसुदेवसुताव् उभौ ॥ उद्यानेषु विचित्रेषु फलपुष्पावनामिषु । चेरतुः सुमहात्मानौ यादवैः परिवारितौ ॥ एवं ताव् एकनिर्माणौ मथुरायां शुभाननौ । रामकृष्णौ समालिङ्ग्य यदुभिश् चानुमोदितः । वसुदेवाभ्यनुज्ञातः स्वम् एव शकटं ययौ । सूतः एतद् वो बालचरितं सकलं मुनिपुंगवाः । कस्य चित् त्व् अथ कालस्य राजा राजगृहेश्वरः । शुश्राव निहतं कंसं जरासंधः प्रतापवान् ॥ अस्तिः प्राप्तिश् च कंसस्य महिष्यौ भरतर्षभ । आजगाम षडङ्गेन बलेन महता वृतः । कृष्णस्य वधम् अन्विच्छन् मधुराम् अन्ववर्तत । अस्तिः प्राप्तिश् च नाम्नास् तां मागधस्य सुते नृप । उभे कंसस्य ते भार्ये प्रादाद् बार्हद्रथो नृपः ॥
units.english: Thereupon in an auspicious moment ascending a car drawn by horses, Janārddana, the slayer of his enemies, entered the city of Mathurā. As the gods follow Sakra so all the Yadavas followed Upendra when he entered the charming city of Mathurā. Thereafter as the sun and moon enter into the setting mountain so those two descendants of Yadu delightedly entered into Vasudevā's house. Keeping all their arms in their own house those high-souled sons of Vasudeva, ranging at will along with the Yādavas, began to range in woods full of fruits and flowers and in streamlets of clear water near the Raivata mountain beautified with lotus leaves and Kārandavas. Thus Rāma and Keshava, of beautiful faces and having one heart enjoyed there a few days under Ugrasena –. Vaishampayana said:—United with Rohini's son Krishna spent some days happily in the city of Mathura filled with Yādavas. Gradually his person was embellished with the grace of youth and regal prosperity and he began to range all over Mathurā adorned with woods. After some days had elapsed in this way, Jarāsandha, the king of Rājagriha, heard of Kansa's death from his two daughters. Hearing this the powerful Jarāsandha was worked up with anger. And in order to pay his debt to Kansa and to slay all the Yadus, the powerful Jarāsandha, in no time, set out with his army consisting of six divisions. king, the king of Magadha had two very beautiful and youthful daughters by name Asti and Prāpti. The royal son of Varhadratha conferred them on Kansa –.

units.sanskrit: स ताभ्यां मुमुदे राजा बध्वा पितरम् आहुकम् । समाश्रित्य जरासंधम् अनादृत्य च यादवान् । शूरसेनेश्वरो राजा यथा ते बहुशो श्रुतः ॥
units.english: Having chained his father the son of Ahuka enjoyed in their company. You have heard many a time and oft how, depending on Jarāsandhā's help and disregarding the Yadavas the lord of Surasena became king.

units.sanskrit: ज्ञातिकार्यार्थसिद्ध्यर्थम् उग्रसेनहिते स्थितः । वसुदेवो ऽभवन् नित्यं कंसो न ममृषे च तम् ॥
units.english: In order to satisfy his duties by his kinsmen and to accomplish their objects Vasudeva was always carefully engaged in Ugrasena's well-being. Kansa did not spare him even.

units.sanskrit: रामकृष्णौ व्यपाश्रित्य हते कंसे दुरात्मनि । उग्रसेनो ऽभवद् राजा भोजवृष्ण्यन्धकैर् वृतः ॥
units.english: When the vicious-souled Kansa was slain by Ramā and Krishna, Ugrasena, encircled by Bhojas, Vrishnis and Andhakas, became king.

units.sanskrit: दुहितृभ्यां जरासंधः प्रियाभ्यां बलवान् नृपः । यदुराजधानीं मथुरां रोद्धुम् अभ्यागतो नृपः । कृत्वा सर्वसमुद्योगं क्रोधाद् अभिययौ यदून् ॥
units.english: Asti and Prāpti, the wives of a hero, were the beloved daughters of king Jarāsandha. Therefore burning like fire in anger at their instigation and making every possible arrangement the king of Magadha started for Mathurā.

units.sanskrit: दुर्योधनादयश् चैव धार्तराष्ट्रा महाबलाः । एते चान्ये च राजानो बलवन्तो महारथाः । तम् अन्वयुर् जरासंधं विद्विषन्तो जनार्दनम् ॥
units.english: All the highly energetic warrior kings who were defeated and subjugated by Jarāsandha’s prowess, all those who were his friends, relatives, kinsmen and allies, encircled by their own armies, followed Jarāsandha with a view to please him.

units.sanskrit: ते शूरसेनान् आविश्य प्रभूतयवसेन्धनान् । ऊषुः संरुध्य मथुरां परिक्षिप्य बलैस् तदा ॥
units.english: Entering the province of Shurasena, abounding in barley and fuels, they all, placing their respecting detachments before them, laid siege to Mathurā -.

units.sanskrit: अपश्यन् वृष्णयः सर्वे पुरस्कृत्य जनार्दनम् ॥ तान् आगतान् नृपान् राजन् मागधान् राजसत्तमान् । ततो हृष्टमनाः कृष्णो रामं वचनम् अब्रवीत् । त्वरते खलु कार्यार्थो देवतानां न संशयः ॥ लक्ष्यन्ते हि ध्वजाग्राणि रथानां वातरंहसाम् ॥ छत्राण्य् आर्य विराजन्ते प्रोच्छ्रितानि सितानि च ॥ अहो नृपरथोदग्रा विमलाश् छत्रपङ्क्तयः । अभिवर्तन्ति नः शुभ्रा यथा खे हंसपङ्क्तयः ॥
units.english: Vaishampayana said:—Holding their counsels all the Yādavas, headed by Janārddana, surveyed the encampment of the kings in the gardens of Mathurā. Afterwards with a delighted heart Krishna said to Rāma:—Forsooth the accomplishment of the object of the gods is near at hand since king Jarāsandha has come near us. The pennons of the cars, coursing like air, are being seen –. Behold, Sir, there shine the umbrellas of kings desirous of victory, white as the moon. The rows, of white umbrellas stationed on the cars of the kings, are moving towards us like swans ranging in the sky.

units.sanskrit: काले खलु नृपः प्राप्तो जरासंधो महीपतिः । आवयोर् युद्धनिकषः प्रथमः समरातिथिः ॥
units.english: However the king Jarāsandha has arrived here in proper time. He is our first guest of battle and is the touch-stone for testing our strength or weakness.

units.sanskrit: आर्य तिष्ठाव सहिताव् अनुप्राप्ते महीपतौ । युद्धारम्भः प्रयोक्तव्यो बलं तावद् विमृश्यताम् ॥
units.english: Sir, while the emperor has arrived here, we must begin with the fight. Judge now the strength of the enemy's army .

units.sanskrit: एवम् उक्त्वा ततः कृष्णः स्वस्थः संग्रामलालसः । जरासंधम् अभिप्रेप्सुश् चकार बलदर्शनम् ॥
units.english: Giving vent to these words without any anxiety, Krishna, desirous of slaying Jarāsandha and fighting with him, began to survey his army.

units.sanskrit: वीक्षमाणश् च तान् सर्वान् नृपान् यदुवरो ऽव्ययः । आत्मानम् आत्मना वाक्यम् उवाच हृदि मन्त्रवित् ॥
units.english: Having taken a survey of the assembled kings and armies, the immortal Krishna, the foremost of Yadus conversant with Mantras began to think within himself.

units.sanskrit: इमे ते पृथिवीपालाः पार्थिवे वर्त्मनि स्थिताः । ये विनाशम् इहेष्यन्ति शास्त्रदृष्टेन कर्मणा ॥
units.english: These are the kings assembled who wend the ways of the mortals and will meet with death on account of their own actions as pointed out by scriptures.

units.sanskrit: प्रोक्षिताः खल्व् इमे मन्ये मृत्युना नृपपुंगवाः । स्वर्गगानि तथा ह्य् एषां वपूंषि प्रचकाशिरे ॥
units.english: consider these leading kings, on the verge of death, sprinkled by Death like unto sacrificial beasts. Their bodies are all shining as if they are about to repair to the celestial region.

units.sanskrit: एषां नृपतिमुख्यानां बलौघैर् अभिपीडिता । भूमिर् निरन्तरा चेयं बलराष्ट्राभिसंवृता ॥
units.english: Assailed by the armies of these sovereigns and exhausted with the weight of their burden Prithivi earth, covered with powerful kingdoms, went to Brahmā in the celestial region.

units.sanskrit: भविष्यति नरेन्द्रौघैः शतशो विनिपातितैः ॥
units.english: In no time the surface of the earth will be shorn of men -. And kings by hundreds will be killed.

units.sanskrit: नराधिपसहस्रौघैर् अनुयातो महाद्युतिः ॥
units.english: Innumerable kings attentively followed him.

units.sanskrit: व्यायतोदग्रतुरगैः सयन्त्रैः सुसमाहितैः । रथैः सांग्रामिकैर् युक्तैर् असङ्गगतिभिः क्व चित् ॥ हेमकक्ष्यैर् महाघण्टैर् वारणैर् वारिदोपमैः । महामात्रोत्तमारूढैः कल्पितै रणकोविदैः ॥
units.english: All the quarters of the city and her woods, resounding with the rattle of cars resembling the muttering of clouds, the tinkling of the ornaments worn by elephants in rut, the neighings of the horses and the leonine shouts of the infantry, the Emperor Jarāsandha, with his army, appeared like an ocean. With shouts and slapping of arms, the armies of these kings, consisting of proud warriors, appeared like an army of clouds.

units.sanskrit: रथैः पवनसंपातैर् गजैश् च जलदोपमैः । तुरगैश् च जवोपेतैः पत्तिभिः खगमैर् इव ॥ सबलास् ते महीपाला जरासंधपुरोगमाः । परिवार्य पुरीं सर्वे निवेशायोपचक्रिरे ॥
units.english: That army, consisting of cars and infuriated elephants, quick-coursing horses, and infantry resembling the sky-rangers, appeared like a collection of clouds descending on the ocean in the rains -. Thereupon all the kings, headed by Jarāsandha, with their armies encamped around the city of Mathurā.

units.sanskrit: शुक्लपर्यन्तपूर्णस्य यथा रूपं महोदधेः ॥
units.english: The detachments of the army accomodated in the tents shone like the ocean overflowing in the light half of the month.

units.sanskrit: वीतरात्रे ततः काले समुत्तस्थुर् महीक्षितः । आरोहणार्थं पुर्यास् ते समीयुर् युद्धलालसाः ॥ समवायीकृताः सर्वे यमुनाम् अनु ते नृपाः । तेषां सुतुमुलः शब्दः शुश्रुवे पृथिवीक्षिताम् । तेषां सकञ्चुकोष्णीषाः स्थविरा वेत्रपाणयः । चेरुर् मा शब्द इत्य् एवं ब्रुवन्तो राजशसनात् ॥ तस्य रूपं बलस्यासीन् निःशब्दस्तिमितस्य वै । लीनमीनग्रहस्येव निःशब्दस्य महोदधेः ॥ निःशब्दस्तिमिते तस्मिन् योगाद् इव महार्णवे । जरासंधो बृहद् वाक्यं बृहस्पतिर् इवाददे ॥ सर्वतो नगरी चेयं जनौघैः परिवार्यताम् ॥ कार्या भूमिः समा सर्वा जलौघैश् च परिप्लुता । ऊर्ध्वं चापानि वाह्यन्तां प्रासा वै तोमरास् तथा ॥ दार्यतां चैव टङ्कौघैः खनित्रैश् च पुरी द्रुतम् । नृपश् च युद्धमार्गज्ञा विन्यस्यन्ताम् अदूरतः ॥
units.english: After the expiration of the night those kings, desirous of fighting, rose up for entering into the city. Those kings, assembled on the bank of the Yamunā, began, out of curiosity, to hold proper counsels on the eve of the battle. Then there was heard a great tumult of the kings resembling that of the heaving deep at the time of the universal dissolution. At the command of the king, elderly guards, with head-gears on their heads and canes in their hands, began to move about exclaiming Ma. Do not make noise. Thereupon that army, hushed into silence, shone like an ocean abounding in fishes and huge serpents. When informed of the mandate of the king that huge ocean-like army stood motionless and silent like a Yogin, the king Jarāsandha, spoke, like Vrihaspati. Let the armies of the kings united lay siege on all sides to this city. Let them get ready stony weapons and maces and let all the level grounds be overflowed with water. Let them hold up swords and daggers. Let them assail the city with Tankas and Khamitras. And let kings, expert in the ways of war, near the city.

units.sanskrit: यावद् एतौ रणे गोपौ वसुदेवसुताव् उभौ । संकर्षणं च कृष्णं च घातयामि शितैः शरैः । आकाशम् अपि बाणौघैर् निःसंपातं यथा भवेत् ॥ मयानुशिष्टास् तिष्ठन्तु पुरीभूमिषु पार्थिवाः । तेषु तेष्व् अवकाशेषु शीघ्रम् आरुह्यतां पुरी ॥ मद्रः कलिङ्गाधिपतिश् चेकितानः सबाह्लिकः । कश्मीरराजो गोनर्दः करूषाधिपतिस् तथा ॥ द्रुमः किंपुरुषश् चैव पार्वतीयष् च दामनः । उलूकः कैतवेयश् च वीरश् चांशुमतः सुतः । एकलव्यो बृहत्क्षत्रः क्षत्रधर्मा जयद्रथः ॥ उत्तमौजाश् च शल्यश् च कौरवाः कैकयास् तथा । त्वरयन्तो ऽभिधावन्तु वाता इव बलाहकान् ॥ अहं च दरदश् चैव चेदिराजश् च संगताः । एवम् एषा पुरी क्षिप्रं समन्ताद् वेष्टिता बलैः । गदिनो ये गदाभिस् ते परिघैः परिघायुधाः । अपरे विविधैः शस्त्रैर् दारयन्तु पुरीम् इमाम् ॥
units.english: As long as do not kill in the battle, with sharpened arrows, the two sons of Vasudeva Krishna and Sangkarshaa, in the guise of milkmen, as long as the sky is not covered with Tankas so long my army should lay seige to the city -. Let all the kings, obeying my command, wait at the outskirts of the city and enter as soon as an opportunity presents itself. Let the Maira king, Kalinga king, Chekitan, the king of Vālhika, Kashmira king Gonarda, the king of Karusha, Druma of Kimpurasha country and the Danava of hill tracts, unitedly and speedily protect the western gate of the city –. Let Ansumāna's son the heroic Kaitaveya, Uluka, Ekalavya, Vrihatkshatra, Kshatrādharmā, Jayadratha, Uttamoujā, Shalya, Kourāvas, Kekayas, Vāmadeva the king of Vidisha, Sāngkiti and the king of Seni occupy the eastern gate of the city. Let them proceed destroying everything as the wind disperses the clouds –. Myself, Darava and the powerful king of Chedi will protect the Southern gate with our army. Thus beseiged on all sides by these armies let the city entertain a great fear like that at the fall of a lightning. Let club-holders with clubs, Parigha-holders with Parighas and other soldiers with various other weapons rend the city.

units.sanskrit: अद्यैव तु नगर्य् एषा विषमोच्चयसंकटा । चतुरङ्गबलं व्यूह्य जरासंधो व्यवस्थितः । अथाभ्ययाद् यदून् क्रुद्धः सह सर्वैर् नराधिपैः । न वै शूरा विकत्थन्ते दर्शयन्त्य् एव पौरुषम् । तद् युद्धम् अभवद् घोरं तेषां देवासुरोपमम् । अल्पानां बहुभिः सार्धं व्यतिषक्तरथद्विपम् ॥
units.english: By you, kings, this city, of up hills and down hills, should be levelled down to-day. Having thus arranged his four-fold forces the king Jarāsandha, along with other kings, proceeded angrily towards the Yādavas. The clever and well-armed warriors Dāshārhas too confronted them. Thus there commenced a terrible fight, abounding in cars and elephants, between that overwhelming army of the kings and the limited number of Yādavas like that between the gods and Asuras.

units.sanskrit: नगरान् निःसृतौ दृष्ट्वा वसुदेवसुताव् उबौ । क्षुब्धं नरवरानीकं त्रस्तसंमूढवाहनम् ॥
units.english: At that time beholding the two sons of Vasudeva issue out of the city the armies of the kings lost heart and the animals grew terrified and bewildered.

units.sanskrit: रथस्थौ दंशितौ चैव चेरतुस् तत्र यादवौ । मकराव् इव संरब्धौ समुद्रक्षोभणाव् उभौ ॥ तयोः प्रयुध्यतोः संख्ये मतिर् आसीद् धृतात्मनोः । आयुधानां पुराणानाम् आदाने कृतलक्षणा ॥ ततः खान् निपतन्ति स्म दीप्तान्य् आहवसंप्लवे । लेलिहानानि दिव्यानि महान्ति सुदृढानि च ॥
units.english: Seated on a car those two descendants of Yadu, Rāma and Krishna, began to move about in anger like two Makaras that agitate the ocean. Thereafter when in perfect sense they began to fight in the battle there arose in them their ancient intelligence regarding the use of weapons. And even in that battle-field there fell down from the sky, strong, flaming and great weapons.

units.sanskrit: क्रव्यादैर् अनुयातानि मूर्तिमन्ति बृहन्ति च । तृषितान्य् आहवे भोक्तुं नृपमांसानि वै भृशम् ॥ दिव्यस्रग्दामधारीणि त्रासयन्ति नभश्चरान् । प्रभया भासमानानि दंशितानि दिशो दश ॥
units.english: In order to feed upon the flesh of the kings, those huge weapons, assuming bodily forms, stricken with thirst as if, adorned with celestial garlands and scents, burning in their own effulgence and terrifying the sky-rangers, descended from the welkin. And Rākshasas, desirous of eating royal flesh, followed them -.

units.sanskrit: हलं संवर्तकं नाम सौनन्दं मुसलं तथा । धनुषां प्रवरं शार्ङ्गं गदा कौमोदकी च ह ॥ चत्वार्य् एतानि तेजांसि विष्णुप्रहरणानि च । ताभ्यां समवतीर्णानि यादवाभ्यां महारणे ॥ जग्राह प्रथमं रामो ललामप्रतिमं हलम् । दर्शनीयं च लोकेषु धनुर् जलदनिस्वनम् । नाम्ना शार्ङ्गम् इति ख्यातं विष्णुर् जग्राह वीर्यवान् ॥ देवैर् निगदितार्थस्य गदा तस्यापरे करे । विषक्ता कुमुदाक्षस्य नाम्ना कौमोदकीति सा ॥
units.english: When in that great battle came down for those two Yadavas, the ploughshare Samvartaka, the mace Sounanda, Srānga the foremost of bows, the club Koumodaki—these four powerful weapons of Vishnu, the beautiful Rāma, the foremost of Sātwatas, took up first of all, with his right hand, the plough-share, embellished with celestial garlands, rising like a flag and proceeding obliquely like a serpent, and that foremost of maces Sounanda that creates depression in the enemy –. The powerful Krishna took up the celebrated bow Srānga which is worthy of being seen by all the worlds. The other hand of the lotus-eyed Krishna, the necessity of whose incarnation was known to the gods, was adorned with the club by name Koumodi.

units.sanskrit: तौ सप्रहरणौ वीरौ साक्षाद् विष्णोस् तनूपमौ । समरे रामगोविन्दौ रिपूंस् तान् प्रत्ययुध्यताम् ॥
units.english: Thus armed the heroic Rāma and Govinda, resembling Vishnu himself, opposed the enemies in battle.

units.sanskrit: द्विषत्सु प्रतिकुर्वाणौ पराक्रान्तौ यथेश्वरौ ॥ विचेरतुर् यथा देवौ वसुदेवसुताव् उभौ । हलम् उद्यम्य रामस् तु सर्पेन्द्रम् इव कोपितः । चचार समरे वीरो द्विषताम् अन्तको यथा ॥ विकर्षन् रथयूथानि क्षत्रियाणां महात्मनाम् । कुञ्जरांल् लाङ्गलक्षिप्तान् मुसलाक्षेपताडितान् । रामो विराजन् समरे निर्ममन्थ यथाचलान् ॥
units.english: Displaying their prowess and discomfitting their enemies those two heroic sons of Vasudeva, dependant on each other and designated by the appellations of elder and younger brothers, began to range there like two gods –. Raising up in anger his plough-share resembling the king of serpents, ranging in the battle-field like the very death of his enemies and drawing in the cars, elephants and steeds of the Kshatriya car-warriors Rāma began to appease his anger –. Throwing up these mountain-like elephants with the end of his plough-share and as if churning them with the strokes of his mace he began to move about in that battle-field.

units.sanskrit: ते विध्यमाना रामेण समरे क्षत्रियर्षभाः । जरासंधान्तिकं वीराः समरार्ताः प्रजग्मिरे ॥ तान् उवाच जरासंधः क्षत्रधर्मे व्यवस्थितः । परावृत्तस्य समरे विरथस्य पलायतः । भ्रूणहत्याम् इवासह्यां प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः ॥
units.english: Thus brought on the point of being almost destroyed by Rāma the leading Kshatriyas returned in fear to Jarāsandha, who, observant of the duties of a Kshatriya, said thus to them:—Fie on your Kshatriya conduct, since you have returned from the battle-field in fear –. The learned say that those, who, deprived of their cars, fly away from the battle-field, are visited by an unbearable sin like that of infanticide.

units.sanskrit: भीताः कस्मान् निवर्तध्वं धिग् एतां क्षत्रवृत्तिताम् । क्षिप्रं समभिवर्तध्वं मम वाक्येन चोदिताः । अथ वा तिष्ठत रथैः प्रेक्षकाः समवस्थिताः । यावद् एतौ रणे गोपौ प्रेषयामि यमक्षयम् ॥
units.english: Why do you fly away, terrified Kshatryas? Fie on your conduct. Urged on by my bows do you return soon. Wait here as spectators. shall myself despatch these two cow-herds to the abode of Yama.

units.sanskrit: ततस् ते क्षत्रियाः सर्वे जरासंधेन चोदिताः । सृजन्तः शरजालानि हृष्टा योद्धुं व्यवस्थिताः ॥
units.english: Thus urged on by Jarāsandha the Kshatriyas again rallied round with delighted hearts. And spreading a net-work of arrows they again engaged in fight.

units.sanskrit: ते हयैः काञ्चनापीडै रथैश् चाम्बुदनादिभिः । नागैश् चाम्भोदसंकाशैर् महामात्रप्रचोदितैः ॥ सतनुत्राः सनिस्त्रिंशाः सपताकायुधध्वजाह्. । स्वारोपितधनुष्मन्तः सुतूणीराः सतोमराः ॥
units.english: Armed with coats of mail, Nishtringshas, pennons, swords, flags, bows with strings, quivers and arrows and accompanied by horses embellished with golden chaplets, cars followed by a rattle like the muttering of clouds and elephants resembling clouds and driven by drivers they again set out for the battle-field –.

units.sanskrit: रणे ते ऽभिगता रेजुः स्यन्दनस्था महीक्षितः ॥ ते युद्धरागा रथिनो व्यगाहन्त युधां वराः । गदाभिश् चैव गुर्वीभिः क्षेपणीयैश् च मुद्गरैः ॥ सुपर्णधजम् आस्थाय कृष्णस् तु रथम् उत्तमम् । तदाभ्ययाज् जरासंधं शरैर् विव्याध चाष्टभिः ॥ सो ऽपि विध्वाष्टभिर् विष्णुम् उग्रसेनं ददर्श ह । तं कृच्छ्रगतम् आज्ञाय चित्रसेनो महारथः । सेनानीः कौशिकश् चैव कृष्णं विव्याधतुः शरैः ॥
units.english: With rising umbrellas held over their heads and fanned by beautiful chowries the kings, stationed on cars, shone greatly in the battle-field. Taking up heavy clubs and maces, some warrior-kings, foremost of car-warriors, out of love for war, entered the battle-field. In the meantime, seated on a most excellent car, adorned with a pennon carrying the emblem of Garuda the powerful Vāsudeva, ever increasing the delight of the celestials, approached carefully Jarāsandha and pierced him with eight arrows, his charioteer with five sharpened shafts and his horses with other arrows. Beholding Jarāsandha in this perilous plight the mighty car-warriors Chitrasena and the Commander-in Chief Kaishika both cut Krishna with arrows.

units.sanskrit: त्रिभिर् विव्याध संसक्तं बलदेवं च कौशिकः । बलदेवो धनुश् चास्य भल्लेनाजौ द्विधाकरोत् । जवेनाभ्यर्दयच् चापि तान् अरीञ् शरवृष्टिभिः ॥
units.english: And Kaishika pierced Baladeva with three arrows –. With his spike the heroic Baladeva sundered his bow into two pieces and creating in no time a downpour of arrows assailed many a hero with his arms embellished with gold.

units.sanskrit: तं चित्रसेनः संरब्धो विव्याध नवभिः शरैः । कौशिकः पञ्चभिश् चापि जरासंधश् च सप्तभिः ॥
units.english: Worked up with anger Chitrasena wounded him with nine arrows -. Then Kaishika wounded him with five arrows and Jarāsandha with seven.

units.sanskrit: त्रिभिस् त्रिभिश् च नाराचैस् तान् बिभेद जनार्दनः । शरैर् दशसहस्रैश् च माधवस्य हि पश्यतः ॥
units.english: Janārddana wounded them each with three winged arrows. The powerful Baladeva struck Chitrasena's car with ten sharpened arrows.

units.sanskrit: बलदेवो धनुश् चाजौ भल्लेनास्य द्विधाकरोत् ॥
units.english: Baladeva, with his spike, sundered his bow into two pieces.

units.sanskrit: स च्छिन्नधन्वा विरथो गदाम् आदाय वीर्यवान् । अभ्यद्रवत् सुसंक्रुद्धो जिघांसुर् मुसलायुधम् ॥
units.english: With his bow shattered and deprived of his car, the powerful Chitrasena, greatly worked up with anger and desirous of slaying the holder of plough-share, proceeded towards him.

units.sanskrit: सिसृक्षतस् तु नाराचांश् चित्रसेनवधैषिणः । धनुश् चिच्छेद रामस्य जरासंधो महाबलः । गदया च जघानाश्वान् कोपात् स मगधेश्वरः ॥
units.english: The highly powerful Jarāsandha cut off the bow of Rāma who was discharging Nārāchas in order to kill Chitrasena –. The king of Magadha, in anger, struck his horses with his club.

units.sanskrit: रामं चाभ्यद्रवद् वीरो जरासंधो महाबलः । आदाय मुसलं रामो जरासंधम् उपाद्रवत् । तयोस् तु युद्धम् अभवत् परस्परवधैषिणोः ॥
units.english: The highly powerful and heroic Jarāsandha thus confronted Rāma. Then taking up a mace Rāma pursued Jarāsandha. An encounter then took place between them both desirous of killing each other.

units.sanskrit: चित्रसेनस् तु संसक्तं दृष्ट्वा रामेण मागधम् । रथम् अन्यं समारुह्य जरासंधम् अवारयत् ॥ उभयोर् अन्तरे ताभ्यां संकुलं समपद्यत । ततः सैन्येन महता जरासंधो ऽभिसंवृतः । रामकृष्णाग्रगान् भोजान् आससाद महाबलः ॥
units.english: Beholding the Magadha king fight with Rāma, Chitrasena, ascending a war-car, encircled Jarāsandha with a huge army of elephants and other warriors. Then began a close fight between the two armies -. Thereupon surrounded by his huge army the highly powerful Jarāsandha attacked the Yādavas who preceded Rāma and Krishna.

units.sanskrit: प्रादुर् बभूव तुमुलः सेनयोर् उभयोस् तयोः ॥
units.english: Then there arose a great tumult from both the armies like that of an agitated ocean.

units.sanskrit: उभयोः सेनयो राजन् प्रादुर् आसीन् महास्वनः ॥
units.english: king, there was heard a great sound of the numberless bugles, conches and trumpets of both the armies.

units.sanskrit: क्ष्वेडितास्फोटितोत्क्रुष्टैस् तुमुलः सर्वतो ऽभवत् । उत्पपात रजश् चापि खुरनेमिसमुद्धतम् ॥
units.english: On all sides were heard the shouts and the slapping of the arms of the soldiers. And a storm of dust was raised by the hoofs of the horses and the wheels of the cars.

units.sanskrit: समुद्यतमहाशस्त्राः प्रगृहीतशरासनाः । अन्योन्यम् अभिगर्जन्तः शूरास् तत्रावतस्थिरे ॥
units.english: And there stood roaring at one another, heroes armed with bows and various other weapons.

units.sanskrit: रथिनः सादिनश् चैव पत्तयश् च सहस्रशः । गजाश् चातिबलास् तत्र संनिपेतुर् अभीतवत् ॥
units.english: Thereupon giving up all hopes of life, thousands of highly powerful car-warriors, elephant drivers and infantry fearlessly engaged in fight.

units.sanskrit: वृष्णीभिः सह योधानां जरासंधस्य दारुणः ॥
units.english: And a terrible encounter took place between Jarāsandha's army and the Yādavas -.

units.sanskrit: ततः शिनिर् अनाधृष्टिर् बभ्रुर् विपृथुर् आहुकः । बलदेवं पुरस्कृत्य सैन्यस्यार्धेन दंशिताः ॥ दक्षिणं पक्षम् आसेदुः शत्रुसैन्यस्य भारत । सृजन्तः शरवर्षाणि समभित्यक्तजीविताः ॥ भीष्मकेणाभिगुप्तस्य रुक्मिणा च महात्मना । देवकेनापि राजेन्द्र तथा मद्रेश्वरेण च । प्राच्यैश् च दाक्षिणात्यैश् च गुप्तवीर्यबलान्वितैः ॥
units.english: Bhārata, placing Baladeva before them and taking a half of their army Sini, Anādhrishthi, Babhra, Vipritha and Ahuka attacked the sothern flank of the enemy's army protected by Jarāsandha, the king of Chedis, the highly powerful Udichya, Salya, Sālya and other kings. And renouncing all hopes of life they began to discharge arrows –. foremost kings, Avagāha, Prithu, Kanka, Satadyumna and Viduratha, led by Janārddana, with the other half of the army attached the detachment protected by the highly powerful Bhishmaka, Rukshmi, Devaka, the Madra king and the kings of the West and South endued with energy and prowess.

units.sanskrit: तेषां युद्धं समभवत् समभित्यक्तजीवितम् । शक्त्यृष्टिप्रासबाणौघान् सृजतां तुमुलं महत् ॥
units.english: And casting off all hopes of life they began a dreadful fight discharging, Saktis, Rishthis, Prāsas and arrows –.

units.sanskrit: सात्यकिश् चित्रकः श्यामो युयुधानश् च वीर्यवान् । राजाधिदेवो मृदुरः श्वफल्कश् च महाबलः ॥ सत्राजिच् च प्रसेनश् च बलेन महता वृताः । भीरूणां त्रासजननं यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनम् । राजभिश् चापि बहुभिर् वेणुदारिमुखैः सह ॥
units.english: On that battle encircled by a huge army Salyaki, Chitraka, Shyāma, the energetic Yuyudhāna, Rajādhideva, Mridara, the mighty car-warriors Swaphalka, Prasena, and Satrajit, attacked the left flank of the enemy's army. They began to fight there attacking half of the enemy's army led by Mridara and assisted by the highly powerful western kings headed by Venudari and the sons of Dhritarāshtra -.

units.sanskrit: वैशंपायन उवाच ततो युद्धानि वृष्णीनां बभूव सुमहान्त्य् अथ । मागधस्य महामात्यैर् नृपैश् चैवानुयायिभिः ॥
units.english: Vaishampayana said:—Thereupon there commenced a great battle between the Vrishnis and the commanders and vassal kings of the lord of Magadha.

units.sanskrit: रुक्मिणा वासुदेवस्य भीष्मकस्याहुकेन च । क्राथस्य वसुदेवेन कौशिकस्य च बभ्रुणा । गदेन चेदिराजस्य दन्तवक्त्रस्य शंभुना ॥
units.english: foremost of the descendants of Bharata, Vāsudeva fought with Rukshmi, Ahuka with Bishmaka, Vasudeva with Kratha, Vabhru with Kaishika, the king of Chedi with Gava, and Shambhu with Dantavakra.

units.sanskrit: तथान्यैर् वृष्णिवीराणां नृपाणां च महात्मनाम् । युद्धम् आसीद् धि सैन्यानां सैनिकैर् भरतर्षभ ॥ गजैर् गजा हयैर् अश्वाः पदाताश् च पदातिभिः । रथा रथैर् विमिश्रैश् च योधा युयुधिरे नृप ॥ जरासंधस्य रज्ञस् तु रामेणासीत् समागमः । महेन्द्रस्येव वृत्रेण दारुणो लोमहर्षणः ॥
units.english: Thus did the great heroes and soldiers, belonging to the army of Vrishnis, fight for twenty-seven days with the highly powerful sovereigns and soldiers of the king of Magadha's party -. Those who rode elephants fought with such, the cavalry with the cavalry, the infantry with the infantry and the car-warriors with the car-warriors. dreadful hair-stirring encounter took place between Rāma and Jarāsandha like unto that between Vitra and the king of gods.

units.sanskrit: अवेक्ष्य रुक्मिणीं कृष्णो रुक्मिणं न व्यपोथयत् ॥ ज्वलनार्कांशुसंकाशान् आशीविषविषोपमान् । वारयाम् आस कृष्णो वै शरांस् तस्य तु शिक्षया । अन्येषां सुमहान् आसीद् बलौघानां परिक्षयः । उभयोः सेनयो राजन् मांसशोणितकर्दमः ॥
units.english: Caring for Rukshmini’s feeling Krishna did not slay Rukshmi, but by virtue of his own learning he sent back his shafts burning like the rays of the sun and dreadful like venomous serpents. dreadful onslaught of soldiers took place in this battle -. The battle-field was covered with mud of flesh and blood of both the armies.

units.sanskrit: तस्मिन् विमर्दे योधानां संख्याव्यक्तिर् न विद्यते ॥
units.english: In that encounter of both the contending armies an endless number of headless figures arose from all sides.

units.sanskrit: रथी रामो जरासंधं शरैर् आशीविषोपमैः । आवृन्वन्न् अभ्ययाद् वीरस् तं च राजा स मागधः ॥
units.english: The car-warrior Rāma enveloped Jarāsandha with arrows resembling poisonous serpents. The heroic king of Magadha too covered him with arrows.

units.sanskrit: अन्योन्यं विविधैर् अस्त्रैर् विध्वा विध्वा विनेदतुः । तौ क्षीनशस्त्रौ विरथौ हताश्वौ हतसारथी । गदे गृहीत्वा विक्रान्ताव् अन्योन्यम् अभिधावताम् ॥
units.english: Thereupon approaching each other in quick-coursing cars they struck each other with diverse weapons and sent up leonine shouts. After their horses and charioteers been slain, their cars had been shattered and their weapons fallen short they took up their clubs and ran towards each other.

units.sanskrit: कम्पयन्तौ भुवं वीरौ ताव् उद्यतमहागदौ । ददृशाते महात्मानौ गिरी सशिखराव् उभौ ॥
units.english: Taking up their clubs in anger those two highly powerful heroes, expert in fighting with clubs and having arms as huge as mountain summits, ran towards each other.

units.sanskrit: व्युपारमन्त युद्धानि प्रेक्षन्तौ पुरुषर्षभौ । उभौ तौ परमाचार्यौ लोके ख्यातौ महाबलौ । मत्ताव् इव गजौ युद्धे अन्योन्यम् अभिधावताम् ॥
units.english: And in order to witness their fight other heroes desisted from the encounter. Thereupon those two highly powerful heroes, celebrated in the worlds as the masters of the art of war, began to fight with each other like two infuriated elephants.

units.sanskrit: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश् च परमर्षयः । समन्ततश् चाप्सरसः समाजग्मुः सहस्रशः ॥ तद् देवयक्षगन्धर्व महर्षिभिर् अलंकृतम् । अभिदुद्राव रामं तु जरासंधो महाबलः । सव्यं मण्डलम् आवृत्य बलदेवस् तु दक्षिणम् ॥
units.english: king, thereupon came there from all quarters thousands and thousands of gods Gandharvas, Siddhas, Saints and Yakshas. Shining greatly in their effulgence the battle-field looked like welkin covered with luminous bodies –. Then turning toward left the highly powerful Jarāsandha ran towards Rāma and Baladava too turned towards south.

units.sanskrit: तौ प्रजह्रुर् अन्योन्यं गदायुद्धविशारदौ । दन्ताभ्याम् इव मातङ्गौ नादयन्तौ दिशो दश ॥
units.english: By resounding ten quarters as an elephant strikes his antagonist with his tusks so those two heroes, skilled in club fighting, struck each other.

units.sanskrit: गदानिपातो रामस्य शुश्रुवे ऽशनिनिस्वनः । जरासंधस्य चरणे पर्वतस्येव दीर्यतः ॥
units.english: In that encounter the sound of the fall of the Baladeva's club was heard like that of thunder-bolt, and that of Magadha king's club was like the riving of a mountain.

units.sanskrit: न स्म कम्पयते रामं जरासंधकरच्युता । गदा गदाभृतां श्रेष्ठं विन्ध्यं गिरिम् इवाचलम् ॥
units.english: As the wind cannot agitate the mount Vindhya so the club, slipped off the hands of Jarāsandha, could not shake the foremost of the holders of club.

units.sanskrit: रामस्य तु गदावेगं वीर्यात् स मगधेश्वरः । सेहे धैर्येण महता शिक्षया च व्यपोहयत् ॥
units.english: By virtue of learning and patience Jarāsandha, the king of Magadha, bore and withstood the velocity of Rāma's club.

units.sanskrit: एवं तौ तत्र संग्रामे विचरन्तौ महाबलौ । समाश्वास्य मुहूर्तं तु पुनर् अन्योन्यम् आहताम् ॥
units.english: Thus moving about in diverse circles in the battle-field for a long time both of them grew tired. And then taking rest for some time they began to strike each other again –.

units.sanskrit: एवं तौ योधमुख्यौ तु समं युयुधतुश् चिरम् । न च तौ युद्धवैमुख्यम् उभाव् एव प्रजग्मतुः ॥
units.english: Those two foremost of warriors fought with each other for some time on equal terms. And none of them left the battle-field.

units.sanskrit: अथापश्यद् गदायुद्धे विशेषं तस्य वीर्यवान् । रामः क्रुद्धो गदां त्यक्त्वा जग्राह मुसलोत्तमम् ॥
units.english: Thereupon witnessing Jarāsandha's efficiency in club-fighting the powerful Rama left off his club in anger and took up his mace.

units.sanskrit:
तम् उद्यतं तदा दृष्ट्वा मुसलं घोरदर्शनम् । अमोघं बलदेवेन क्रुद्धेन तु महारणे ।
क्रुद्धो ऽथ रामभद्रस् तु गदया तं जगाम ह ।
जरासंधो ऽथ गदया बलभद्रं समाहनत् ॥
ततः क्रुद्धो जरापुत्रस् ताडयाम् आस वक्षसि ।
समादीप्तौ तु राजेन्द्र विरथौ विधनुर्धरौ ॥ गदाहतौ महावीरौ केवलौ युद्धरङ्गिनौ ।
शुशुभाते गदाहस्तौ परस्परवधैषिणौ ॥
द्वाव् एव मृत्यू राजेन्द्र संगताव् इव शोभितौ ॥ ततः क्रुद्धो हलधरश् छेत्तुम् ऐच्छज् जरासुतम् ।
ऊरू च पोथयाम् आस गदया राजसंसदि ॥ ऊर्वो रक्तं समापेदे मज्जा समभवत् ततः । ततो हली जरासंधं शिरश् छेत्तुम् उदैक्षत ।
ततो ऽन्तरिक्षे वाग् आसीत् सुस्वरा लोकसाक्षिणी । अचिरेणैव कालेन प्राणांस् त्यक्ष्यति मागधः ॥ जरासंधस् तु तच् छ्रुत्वा विमनाः समपद्यत । न प्रजह्रे ततस् तस्मै पुनर् एव हलायुधः । तौ व्युपारमतां चैव वृष्णयस् ते च पार्थिवाः ॥
units.english: When in that great battle Baladeva, in anger, took up the terrible-looking mace of sure aim there was heard in the sky a sweet voice of the witness of the world which said to Baladeva the holder of plough-share –. Rāma, thou the conferrer of honors, this king of Magadha is not to be slain by thee. Jarasandha shall, in no time, meet with his death from the means that have laid out for his destruction. Hearing this voice of Providence Jarāsandha lost heart and Baladeva did not strike him therefore. Emperor, while they thus desisted from fighting there took place a highly terrible encounter extending over a long time between the Yadavas and other kings in which they struck one. another fiercely. When the Emperor Jarāsandha was thus defeated and took to his heels and when the sun set the highly powerful Yadavas, protected by Krishna, who had gained their aim, did not pursue him in night. And gathering their respective soldiers according to the will of Mādhava they entered into their own city. And all the weapons that came down from the welkin also disappeared -. And filled with absent-mindedness, king Jarāsandha too returned to his own city. And the kings, who followed him, returned to their respective kingdoms. On the other hand, foremost of kings, having defeated Jarāsandha the Yādavas could not consider themselves as completely above defeat, for he was a highly powerful king. The great car warriors Yādavas fought with him for eighteen times and still they could not slay him in the battle-field. The Vrishnis were very few in number and so they were overpowered by the king Vārhadratha who was followed by other kings.

units.sanskrit: जरासंधेन सहिता विप्रजग्मुर् यथागतम् । पराजिते त्व् अपक्रान्ते जरासंधे महीपतौ । वृष्णयश् च महाभागाः कृष्णसंकर्षणाश्रयाः । समानीय स्वसैन्यं तु लब्धलक्ष्या महाबलाः । पुरीं प्रविविशुर् हृष्टाः केशवेनाभिपूजिताः ॥
units.english: Having thus defeated Jarāsandha the king of Magadha, the great car-warriors Vrishnis began to live happily. Vaishampayana said:—With Rohini's son the powerful Vasudeva began to live happily in the city of Mathura filled with Yādavas. Gradually his person shone greatly in the beauty of youth and regal prosperity.

units.sanskrit: जरासंधो ऽपि नृपतिर् विमनाः स्वपुरं ययौ । राजानश् चानुगा ये ऽस्य स्वराष्ट्राण्य् एव ते ययुः । जरासंधं तु ते जित्वा मन्यन्ते नैव तं जितम् । वृष्णयः कुरुशार्दूल राजा ह्य् अतिबलः स वै ॥ को नाम हि जरासंधं रणे जेतुं महीपतिः । शक्नुयाल् लोकविख्यातः साक्षाद् अपि शतक्रतुः । दश चाष्टौ च संग्रामाञ् जरासंधस्य यादवाः । ददुर् न चैनं समरे हन्तुं शेकुर् महारथाः ॥ कृष्णस् तु समरे राजञ् शक्तिमान् अपि मागधम् । अन्यो मृत्युर् इति ज्ञात्वा न च हिंसितवान् प्रभुः । अक्षौहिण्यो हि तस्यासन् विंशतिर् भरतर्षभ । जरासंधस्य नृपतेस् तदर्थं याः समागताः ॥ अल्पत्वाद् अभिभूतास् तु वृष्णयो भरतर्षभ । बार्हद्रथेन राजेन्द्र राजभिः सहितेन वै ॥
units.english: And delightedly he began to range in Mathurā adorned with woods. Once again incited by his two daughters and remembering the death of Kansa, Jarāsandha, the king of Rajagriha, made preparations for a battle. In this wise the mighty car-warriors Yādavas fought seventeen times with Jarāsandha but could not kill him in battle. Out of shame for his previous defeats and with a view to slay Krishna, the highly-powerful and valiant king of Rajagriha the beautiful Emperor Jarāsandha, like unto the king of gods in prowess, set out encircled by a huge army. And despite his many endeavours he again came back unsuccessful -. Hearing that Jarāsandha had desisted the Yadavas, stricken with his fear, began to hold counsels. There upon the highly effulgent Vikadru, well-read in moral laws, said to the lotus-eyed Krishna in the very presence of Ugrasena. my child Govinda, listen to the origin of our family. Listen, shall describe at length the origin of this race of Yadavas as related by Vyasa conversant with the knowledge of spirit. In Manu's race flourished a celebrated and prosperous king by name Haryashwa born of Ikshwāku, and powerful like Mahendra himself.

units.sanskrit: वधश् चैव शृगालस्य करवीरपुरोत्तमे । तत्सुतस्याभिषेकश् च नागराणां च सान्त्वनम् । तत्पत्नीनां प्रलापश् च शक्रदेवाभिषेचनम् । युद्धं सर्वैर् नरेन्द्रैश् च यादवानां महात्मनाम् । मथुरायां प्रवेशश् च कीर्तनीयः सुरैर् अपि । प्रतिष्ठिता च वसुधा शङ्किताः सर्वपार्थिवाः ॥
units.english: Having installed Shrigāla’s son in the city of Karavira Krishana desired to go away on the very day -. All the traders, subjects, ministers and the boys and old men of Mathurā came out to recieve them. As the gods follow Shakra the Yādavas followed Rāma and Govinda to the charming city. Thereupon bowing unto the feet of Vasudeva they showed proper honor to king Ugrasena and other leading Yadavas who were assembled there. They, too, welcomed by them duly in return, delightedly entered into their mother's appartment. Welcome to thee, thou of large arms, descendant of Yadu.

units.sanskrit: तव चागमनं दृष्ट्वा सभाग्याः स्म यथा पुरा । तेन स्म परितुष्टाश् च हृषिताश् च सबान्धवाः ॥ प्रत्युवाच ततो रामः सर्वांस् तान् अभितः स्थितान् । यादवेष्व् अपि सर्वेषु भवन्तो मम बान्धवाः ॥
units.english: thou of a pure countenance, no sooner we desired for thy arrival than thou hadst come and seen us. By it the earth has been established and all the kings have been brought to subjection. Rāma then replied to all the Gopas stationed around him saying:—You are our better friends than even the Yādavas.

units.sanskrit: सहास्माभिर् गतं बाल्यं सहास्माभी रतं वने । गृहेषु भवतां भुक्तं गावश् च परिरक्षिताः । अस्माकं बान्धवाः सर्वे भवन्तो बद्धसौहृदाः ॥
units.english: We had been reared by you and spent our boyhood in sporting here. We took our meals in your houses and tended the kine. You all are our firm friends.

units.sanskrit: एवं भुवति सत्त्वं वै गोपमध्ये हलायुधे । संहृष्टवदनास् तत्र बभूवुर् गोपयोषितः । ततो वनान्तरगतो रेमे रामो महाबलः ॥ एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे गोपा रामाय विदितात्मने । सो ऽपिबत् पाण्डुराभ्राभस् तत्कालं ज्ञातिभिर् वृतः । वनान्तरगतो रामः पानं मदसमीरणम् ॥
units.english: When Halāyudha gave vent to these words in the midst of Gopas, marks of joy were visible on the faces of their women. Thereupon repairing to the forest, the highly powerful Rāma, conversant with the knowledge of spirit, began to sport there with Gopa women. Then the milk-men, conversant with the knowledge of time and place, brought Vāruni wine to him. Rāma, of the hue of a pale cloud, drank that wine in the forest along with his friends.

units.sanskrit: उपजह्रुस् ततस् तस्मै वन्यानि विविधानि च । प्रत्यग्ररमणीयानि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च ॥
units.english: Thereafter the cow-herds brought to him diverse beautiful forest fruits, flowers, meat, sweet juice and full blown lotuses and lilies just collected.

units.sanskrit: श्रवणैकावलम्बेन कुण्डलेन विराजता ॥ चन्दनागरुशीतेन वनमालावलम्बिना । विबभाव् उरसा रामः कैलासेनेव मन्दरः ॥ रराज वपुषा शुभ्रः शशीव घनमालया ॥ लाङ्गलेनावसक्तेन भुजगाभोगवर्तिना । तथा भुजाग्रश्लिष्टेन मुसलेन च भास्वता ॥ स मत्तो बलिनां श्रेष्ठो रराजाघूर्णिताननः । शैशिरीष्व् इव रात्रीषु यथा खेदालसः शशी ॥ स मत्तो यमुनाम् आह स्नातुम् इच्छे महानदि । इहैव माभिगच्छस्व रूपिणी सागरंगमे ॥ संकर्षणस्य मत्तोक्तां भारतीं परिभूय सा । नाभ्यवर्तत तं देशं स्त्रीस्वभावेन मोहिता ॥ ततश् चुक्रोध बलवान् रामो मदसमीरितः । चकार च हलं हस्ते कर्षणाधोमुखं बली ॥
units.english: As the mount Mandara is adorned by the Kailāga hill so Rāma shone, with Kundalas hanging from his cars, with diadem placed a little askance, with locks and head and breast besmeared with sandal and decked with garlands of wild flowers. Clad in an apparel dark-blue like a cloud his white person appeared like the moon enshrouded by darkness. The plough-share, attached to his hands like the hood of a serpent and the burning mace fixed to his finger, increased his beauty the more. Thus with his eyes rolling in intoxication, Rāma, the foremost of the strong, began to enjoy there like the moon in an autumnal night -. Thereupon Rāma said to Yamunā:— great river, going to the ocean, wish to marry you by bathing in your water; come to me therefore in your bodily form. Out of her womanish habit and ignorance Yamunā disregarded his words as being the out-come of drunkenness and did not come to him. Thereat filled with anger and maddened with drunkenness the powerful Rāma took up his plough share and sat with his head looking down in order to drag her.

units.sanskrit: मुमुचुः पुष्पकोशैश् च स्वं रजोरञ्जितं जलम् ॥
units.english: The garland of flowers, that fell down on earth, began to pour, through the leaves, clear water.

units.sanskrit: स हलेनानन्ताग्रेण तीरे गृह्य महानदीम् । चकर्ष यमुनां रामो व्युत्थितां वनिताम् इव ॥ सा विह्वलजलस्रोता ह्रदप्रस्थितसंचया । व्यावर्तत नदी भीता हलमार्गानुसारिणी ॥ लाङ्गलाकृष्टमार्गा सा वेगवक्रानुगामिनी । संकर्षणभयत्रस्ता योषेवाकुलतां गता ॥
units.english: There upon bending down the head of his plough-share Rāma began to drag the bank of the great river like unto a wife following her inclination. At that time the currents of the river were upset and all the fishes and the acquatic animals grew bewildered. Dragged with force by Rāma the powerful river Yamunā, going to the ocean, like unto a drunk woman going astray in a high-road and over whelmed with fear, began to follow the way pointed out by the plough-share.

units.sanskrit: स्रोतःपुलिनबिम्बोष्ठी मृदितैस् तोयताडितैः । फेनमेखलसूत्रैश् च चिह्नैस् तीरानुहासिभिः ॥ तरंगविषमापीडा चक्रवाकोन्मुखस्तनी । वेगगम्भीरवक्राङ्गी त्रस्तमीनवहंगमा ॥ सा तु हंसेक्षणापाङ्गी काशक्षौमोज्झिताम्बरा । उन्मार्गानीतमार्गा सा येन वृन्दावनं वनम् ॥
units.english: She had the bank for her hip, dark-blue lotuses for her lips, the foams driven by the water for her girdle, the grave currents for her moving limbs, the bewildered fishes for her ornaments, the white geese for glances, the rising Kāsa flowers for her silken raiment, the trees grown on her back for the ends of her hairs, the current for her slippery gait, and the mark of the plough-share for the outer corner of her eye, and the Chakravakas for her breast. Although she goes by the lower ground she was made to go up and brought to the forest of Vrindavana -.

units.sanskrit: रोरूयमाणैः खगमैर् अन्विता तीरवासिभिः ॥ सा यदा समतिक्रान्ता नदी वृन्दावनं वनम् । ततः स्त्रीविग्रहा भूत्वा यमुना रामम् अब्रवीत् ॥ प्रसीद राम भीतास्मि प्रतिलोमेन कर्मणा । विपरीतम् इदं रूपं तोयं च मम जायते ॥
units.english: When the river Yamunā was brought to Vrindāvana the water-fowls, as if weeping, followed her. When she crossed the forest of Vrindāvana, Yamunā, assuming the form of a woman, said to Rāma :—Be propitiated with me, lord. have been terrified at these thy unfavourable actions. Behold, this my watery form has been changed.

units.sanskrit: रौहिणेय हसिष्यति मां नन्दः संगता त्वया । कर्षणेन महाबाहो स्वमार्गव्यभिचारिणी ॥
units.english: thou of large arms, son of Rohini, thou hast dragged me away from my own path. Therefore have become unchaste amongst the rivers.

units.sanskrit: प्राप्तां मां सागरे नूनं सपत्न्यो वेगगर्विताः । फेनहासैर् हसिष्यन्ति तोयव्यावृत्तगामिनीम् ॥
units.english: When shall go to the ocean, other rivers, co-wives with me, proud of their course, will smile at me, with their foams and call me an unchaste river.

units.sanskrit: प्रसादं कुरु मे वीर याचे त्वां कृष्णपूर्वज । सुप्रसन्नमना नित्यं भवस्व त्वं सुरोत्तम । कर्षणायुधकृष्टास्मि रोषो ऽयं विनिवर्त्यताम् ॥ एषा मूर्ध्नाभिगच्छामि चरणौ ते हलायुध । मार्गम् आदिष्टम् इच्छामि क्व गच्छामि महाभुज ॥
units.english: Show me the favour, hero, beg thee, elder brother, of Krishna. Be thou delighted at heart, foremost of the celestials. have been dragged here with thy weapon. Do thou assuage thy ire. thou of large arms, thou, the wielder of plough-share, fall at thy feet. Do thou command me, by what path shall go.

units.sanskrit: ताम् एवं ब्रुवतीं द्र्ष्ट्वा यमुनां लाङ्गलायुधः । प्रत्युवाचार्णववधूं मदाक्रान्तालसो बलः ॥ लाङ्गलाकृष्टमार्गा त्वम् इमं मे प्रियदर्शने । शान्तिं व्रज महाभागे गम्यतां च यथासुखम् । लोका हि यावत् स्थास्यन्ति तावत् स्थास्यति मे यशः ॥
units.english: Beholding Yamunā, the wife of the ocean fallen at his feet the holder of plough-share, inebriate with wine, said –:— beautiful Yamunā of fair eye-brows, auspicious damsel seeking union with the ocean, command thee to follow the way pointed out by my plough-share and water this province. Be thou at peace, noble one, and do thou proceed at thy pleasure –. As long as the world will exist my glory will flourish.

units.sanskrit: सागरानिलसंवीतं सागराम्बुनिषेवितम् । विषयं सिन्धुराजस्य शोभितं पुरलक्षणैः ॥
units.english: That city is situate in an extensive watery province of the ocean. And then they enjoyed there like two immortals in the city of the celestials -.

units.sanskrit: ते रक्तसूर्ये दिवसे तत्र यादवपुंगवाः । निवेशाय मतिं चक्रुः कृष्णस्यानुमते स्थिताः । सेनापालाश् च संचक्रुः स्कन्धावारनिवेशनम् ॥ ध्रुवाय तत्र न्यवसत् केशवः सह यादवैः । देशे पुरनिवेशाय स यदुप्रवरो विभुः ॥
units.english: Having thus wended a very long distance the leading Yādus reached the bank of the ocean. Having secured such a picturesque site the Yadavas were highly delighted as if they had arrived at the celestial region. Searching for a site where he would lay out a city Krishna, the slayer of inimical heroes, saw an extensive tract of land situated on the bank of the ocean. It was fanned by the sea breeze and was watered by the ocean. Keshava selected that site for his city and the Yādavas also wanted to encamp their soldiers there. With a view to lay out his city there the Lord Krishna, the foremost of Yadus, lived there with them shorn of anxiety.

units.sanskrit: तस्यास्तु विधिवन् नाम वास्तूनि च गदाग्रजः । निर्ममे पुरुषश्रेष्ठो मनसा यादवोत्तमः ॥
units.english: And that foremost of men, the leader of the Yādavas, having Gada as his elder brother, thought in his mind of the names he would give to the various houses in that city -.

units.sanskrit: एवं द्वारवतीं चैव पुरीं प्राप्य सबान्धवाः । सुखिनो न्यवसन् राजन् स्वर्गे देवगणा इव ॥
units.english: king, having thus secured the city of Dwaravati the Yādavas, along with their friends, lived there happily as do the gods in their own city.

units.sanskrit: कृष्णो ऽपि कालयवनं ज्ञात्वा केशिनिषूदनः । जरासंधभयाच् चापि पुरीं द्वारवतीं ययौ ॥
units.english: descendant of Bhārata, thus informed of the approach of Kālayavana Krishna, the slayer of Keshi, set out for the city of Dwāravati, in fear of Jarāsāndha –.

units.sanskrit: जनमेजय उवाच भगवञ् श्रोतुम् इच्छामि विस्तरेण महात्मनः । चरितं वासुदेवस्य यदुश्रेष्ठस्य धीमतः ॥
units.english: Janamejaya said:— reverend sir, wish to listen at length to the history of the high-souled and intelligent Vāsudeva, the foremost of Yadus.

units.sanskrit: वैशंपायन उवाच वृष्णीनाम् अन्धकानां च गुरुर् गार्ग्यो महातपाः । ब्रह्मचारी पुरा भूत्वा न स्म दारान् स विन्दति ॥ गार्ग्यं गोष्ठे द्विजं स्यालः षण्ढम् इत्य् उक्तवान् द्विजः । यदूनां संनिधौ सर्वे जहसुर् यादवास् ततः ॥
units.english: Vaishampāyana said:—The high-minded Gārgya was the preceptor of both the Andhaka and Vrishni races. He always observed the vow of celibacy; and although he had a wife he did not know her. While the eternal Gārgya, who was a master of passions, was thus spending his days this brother-in-law described him as impotent before the king -.

units.sanskrit: स्यालो ऽभिशप्तवान् गार्ग्यम् अपुमान् इति भूपते ॥ सो ऽभिशप्तस् तदा राजन् नगरे त्व् अमितंजये । लिप्सुः पुत्रं ततो गत्वा तपस् तेपे सुदारुणम् ॥
units.english: king, having been thus dishonored in the city of Ajitanjaya and giving up his desire of being united with his wife out of anger for his brother-in-law, Gārgya engaged in hard penances for obtaining a son.

units.sanskrit: ततो द्वादश वर्षाणि सो ऽयश् चूर्णम् अभक्षयत् । रुद्रस् तस्मै वरं प्रादात् समर्थं युधि निग्रहे । वृष्णीनाम् अन्धकानां च सर्वतेजोमयं सुतम् ॥
units.english: And living on pounded iron for twelve years he worshipped Mahādeva, the holder of trident. For this Rudra conferred on him a boon that he would obtain an all powerful son who would be able to discomfit in battle the descendants of the Vishni and Andhaka races –.

units.sanskrit: ततः शुश्राव तं राजा यवनाधिपतिर् वरम् । पुत्रप्रसवजं देवाद् अपुत्रः पुत्रकामुकः ॥ तम् उपानाय्य स नृपः सान्त्वयित्वा द्विजोत्तमम् । गोपाली त्व् अप्सरास् तत्र गोपस्त्रीवेषधारिणी । धारयाम् आस गार्ग्यस्य गर्भं दुर्धरम् अच्युतम् ॥ मानुष्यां गार्ग्यभार्यायां नियोगाच् छूलपाणिनः । स कालयवनो नाम जज्ञे शूरो महाबलः । अपुत्रस्याथ राज्ञस् तु ववृधे ऽन्तःपुरे शिशुः ॥ तस्मिन्न् उपरते राजन् स कालयवनो नृपः । युद्धाभिकामो राजा तु पर्यपृच्छद् द्विजोत्तमम् । वृष्ण्यन्धककुलं तस्य नारदो वै न्यवेदयत् ॥ ज्ञात्वा तु वरदानं तन् नारदान् मधुसूदनः । उपप्रैक्षत तेजस्वी वर्धन्तं यवनेषु तम् ॥
units.english: The king of Yavanas had no son. Hearing of the boon of having a son conferred upon Gārgya, the foremost of the twice-born by Mahādeva, the king brought him over to his own kingdom. And having consoled him he engaged the milk-women to attend him in their own settlement. Having assumed the guise of a milk-woman, an Apsara, Gopāli by name, conceived that dreadful and undecaying embryo through Gārgya -.
